text.arabic_uthmani: وَبَرَزُوا۟ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعًۭا فَقَالَ ٱلضُّعَفَٰٓؤُا۟ لِلَّذِينَ ٱسْتَكْبَرُوٓا۟ إِنَّا كُنَّا لَكُمْ تَبَعًۭا فَهَلْ أَنتُم مُّغْنُونَ عَنَّا مِنْ عَذَابِ ٱللَّهِ مِن شَىْءٍۢ ۚ قَالُوا۟ لَوْ هَدَىٰنَا ٱللَّهُ لَهَدَيْنَٰكُمْ ۖ سَوَآءٌ عَلَيْنَآ أَجَزِعْنَآ أَمْ صَبَرْنَا مَا لَنَا مِن مَّحِيصٍۢ

words.gloss_range: resumptive connective opening that carries the scene forward from the prior claim
words.prose: The opening {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) is light in form but structurally load-bearing: it carries the discourse from the prior assertion of divine capacity into a visible judgment tableau. The word helps the ayah unfold as exposure, plea, counterclaim, and no-escape closure within one continuous scene.

topics.headline: resumptive judgment-scene opening
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah opens as a connected judgment display, not as a disposable new sentence.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows converge on boundary linkage, resumptive coordination, and the four-beat scene arc; no reference evidence blocks that local function.

words.gloss_range: completed collective emergence into exposed public presence before God
words.root_gloss_range: emergence, exposure, and becoming visible; local syntax selects exposed emergence, not mere arrival
words.prose: {{ar:بَرَزُوا۟}} ({{tr:barazū}}) presents a completed plural emergence into exposed visibility, directed by the following lām phrase toward divine presence. The variant passive reading preserves the same exposure scene while shifting agency, so the surviving payoff is public exposure before God rather than simple motion or arrival; the same exposure formula resonates at (14:48) and (40:16).

topics.headline: completed exposure before God
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the group is brought into open visibility before divine presence, with the same exposure formula resonating at (14:48) and (40:16).
topics.reason: Rows about Form I, passive variant, public exposure, distribution, and scene arc are preserved, while the broad root range is narrowed to the locally governed exposure scene.

words.gloss_range: directional/presentational lām attaching emergence to God
words.prose: {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li}}) attaches the emergence to God as direction, presence, and confrontation. Its payoff is small but important: the exposed group does not merely appear; it appears before the divine addressee of the whole scene.

topics.headline: orientation toward divine presence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the emergence is not aimless; it is directed before God as the one in whose presence the scene occurs.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows agree with QAC grammar that this lām marks the relation between emergence and divine presence.

words.gloss_range: divine proper name in genitive after the lām, anchoring exposure before God
words.root_gloss_range: proper-name field with worship/attachment associations; local grammar selects the divine name in genitive
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}) is governed by the preceding lām and anchors the exposure scene in divine presence. The broader worship and attachment notes remain background; locally the word begins a threefold divine-name frame that later attaches punishment and then guidance to God.

topics.headline: first divine-name anchor
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the divine name first anchors exposure, then returns around punishment and guidance in the ayah.
topics.reason: The rows about genitive case, name recurrence, and etymological pressure survive, with etymology narrowed so it does not replace the local proper-name function.

words.gloss_range: accusative circumstantial totalizer: all together as one exposed group
words.root_gloss_range: gathering, joining, and total aggregation; local form acts as collective circumstance
words.prose: {{ar:جَمِيعًۭا}} ({{tr:jamīʿan}}) functions as an accusative circumstantial totalizer over the exposed group. Its collecting force makes the first tableau comprehensive: all parties are gathered together before the dialogue splits them into weak and arrogant speakers.

topics.headline: all-together exposure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the scene gathers everyone together, so the later dispute begins from shared exposure rather than separate private cases.
topics.reason: Grammar, root semantics, collective form, and scene-position rows all support a totalizing ḥāl reading.

words.gloss_range: immediate sequencing particle from exposure into speech
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) pivots the ayah from the exposed tableau to the first quoted speech. The one-letter particle carries immediate sequence and causal pressure: once everyone is exposed, the weak speak.

topics.headline: pivot from tableau to speech
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the speech follows directly from exposure, as if the tableau immediately generates the dispute.
topics.reason: Rows on taʿqīb, causal pressure, compact form, and dialogue launch are mutually coherent.

words.gloss_range: speech verb opening the weak party’s quoted plea
words.root_gloss_range: saying and speech-report; local use introduces direct quoted speech
words.prose: {{ar:قَالَ}} ({{tr:qāla}}) licenses the weak party’s quoted speech. Its singular form with a plural class makes the weak sound like a collective voice, and it sets up the later plural answer with the second speech verb.

topics.headline: first speech report
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a plural class speaks through a singular report verb, turning the weak into one collective voice.
topics.reason: The rows on singular agreement, quoted complement, speech recurrence, and qāla/qālū echo all survive locally.

words.gloss_range: definite broken plural naming the weak as a recognized class in the dispute
words.root_gloss_range: weakness and doubling; local form names social weakness, not numerical doubling as the main sense
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلضُّعَفَٰٓؤُا۟}} ({{tr:al-ḍuʿafāʾu}}) names a definite broken-plural class: the weak. The root’s doubling associations remain secondary, while the local payoff is social weakness set against self-magnifying leadership; that weak/arrogant confrontation also appears at (7:75-76) and (34:31-33).

topics.headline: the weak as a class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the speakers are not merely described as weak individuals; they are introduced as a recognized class opposite the self-magnifying leaders, a pattern also seen at (7:75-76) and (34:31-33).
topics.reason: Rows on definiteness, broken plural, social opposition, and recurring confrontation scenes are preserved while the root’s doubling branch is kept as background pressure.

words.gloss_range: lām marking the human addressees of the weak party’s speech
words.prose: {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li}}) marks the addressee of the weak party’s speech. It repeats the earlier lām shape but changes the target from divine presence to the human group being confronted.

topics.headline: orientation shifts to leaders
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the orientation shift: after exposure before God, the weak now turn speech toward the human leaders.
topics.reason: The rows on addressee marking, relative-pronoun governance, and contrast with the first lām match the local syntax.

words.gloss_range: definite plural relative pronoun introducing the leaders by the action that defines them
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلَّذِينَ}} ({{tr:alladhīna}}) introduces the relative clause that defines the addressed group by their action. The pronoun does more than point; it lets the following verb supply the moral identity of the leaders.

topics.headline: addressees defined by conduct
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the leaders are identified by what they did, so moral characterization enters before the accusation is spoken.
topics.reason: Rows on definiteness, plural relative form, relative-clause introduction, and moral characterization all align.

words.gloss_range: Form X perfect plural: those who claimed greatness for themselves
words.root_gloss_range: greatness and largeness; Form X locally makes it self-attributed arrogance, not true greatness
words.prose: {{ar:ٱسْتَكْبَرُوٓا۟}} ({{tr:istakbarū}}) is Form X: the leaders made themselves great. The root’s true-greatness field is morally inverted here into self-attributed arrogance, placing them opposite the weak in a recurring dispute pattern at (7:75-76), (34:31-33), and (40:47-48).

topics.headline: self-attributed greatness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the leaders are defined by claimed greatness, an inverted greatness set against the weak in recurring dispute scenes at (7:75-76), (34:31-33), and (40:47-48).
topics.reason: Rows on Form X, estimative reflexive morphology, greatness inversion, party opposition, and recurring punishment dialogues survive, with broad greatness narrowed to arrogant self-claim.

words.gloss_range: emphatic particle opening the weak party’s premise
words.prose: {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:inna}}) opens the weak party’s claim with emphasis. It turns the former following relationship into an asserted premise before the following particle converts that premise into a rescue question.

topics.headline: asserted dependency premise
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the weak do not begin with a question alone; they first assert the old dependency as the basis for the challenge.
topics.reason: Rows on emphatic assertion, premise-before-question sequence, and speech structure are directly supported.

words.gloss_range: past copular verb establishing a shared former state
words.root_gloss_range: being and becoming; local use supplies past state rather than new action
words.prose: {{ar:كُنَّا}} ({{tr:kunnā}}) supplies the past copular frame for the dependency clause. The following predicate tells what they had been, so the word makes the plea rest on a former state of belonging and following.

topics.headline: shared former state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the weak frame their dependence as a past state they inhabited together, not merely as an action they once performed.
topics.reason: Rows on copular grammar, past state, first-person plural form, and the dependency clause are coherent.

words.gloss_range: dative lām relation tying former following to the addressed leaders
words.prose: {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) marks the dative relationship inside the former-dependency claim. The local payoff is not an abstract preposition but a directed relation: the weak were followers in relation to the addressed leaders, which later inverts into the final claim of no possession for us.

topics.headline: following oriented to leaders
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the dependency is aimed toward the leaders: the weak describe their following as a relation bound to those they now confront.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows about dative relation, addressee orientation, pronoun echo, and later inversion survive, while suffix-specific claims are treated as phrase-level pressure around the local lām.

words.gloss_range: collective predicate of former following, with trailing and consequence both in view
words.root_gloss_range: following, trailing behind, and consequence; local masdar names a collective following-condition
words.prose: {{ar:تَبَعًۭا}} ({{tr:tabaʿan}}) is the predicate of the past-state clause and names the weak party’s former condition as collective following. The root keeps trailing and consequence close together: their old social dependence becomes the premise for asking whether the leaders can now avail them.

topics.headline: following as collective condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the weak describe themselves not as isolated followers but as a collective following-condition that grounds their demand for rescue.
topics.reason: Rows on predicate grammar, masdar/collective form, following-consequence semantics, and setup for the rescue question are preserved with the broad root narrowed to local dependence.

words.gloss_range: causal/sequential particle turning the premise into a challenge
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) connects the asserted premise to the rhetorical question. It carries the logic of the weak party’s speech: because we were followers in relation to you, can you now do anything for us?

topics.headline: premise becomes challenge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the question is not random; it follows as the demanded consequence of the claimed former dependence.
topics.reason: Rows on sababiyya, sequence, one-letter transition, and assertion-to-question movement all support the topic.

words.gloss_range: yes/no interrogative opening a challenge about availing capacity
words.prose: {{ar:هَلْ}} ({{tr:hal}}) scopes over the nominal question about availing capacity. In context, it works as a challenge rather than a neutral request for information, with the later indefinite minimum sharpening the expected negative answer.

topics.headline: challenge, not information request
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the weak ask a question already shaped toward failure: can the leaders avail them even the smallest amount?
topics.reason: Rows on interrogative scope, rhetorical challenge, and negative force reinforced by the later minimum object are aligned.

words.gloss_range: independent second-person plural pronoun foregrounding the leaders as questioned subject
words.prose: {{ar:أَنْتُمْ}} ({{tr:antum}}) stands independently before the participial predicate, foregrounding the leaders as the questioned subject. The discourse has moved from describing them as those who self-magnified to facing them directly as you.

topics.headline: leaders directly addressed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the speech turns from third-person identification to direct confrontation: you, the leaders, are now put under question.
topics.reason: Rows on pronoun subject, retained independent form, direct-address shift, and nominal predicate structure support the topic.

words.gloss_range: Form IV active participle asking whether the leaders can avail or make sufficient against punishment
words.root_gloss_range: richness, sufficiency, and availing; local construction selects availing relief, not wealth as possession
words.prose: {{ar:مُّغْنُونَ}} ({{tr:mughnūna}}) is the participial predicate of the question and takes its relief relation through the following prepositional phrases. The broad root can include richness and sufficiency, but here the selected sense is availing: can the leaders make them sufficient against even part of the punishment?

topics.headline: can leaders avail at all
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the weak do not ask for leadership anymore; they test whether the leaders can make any difference against punishment.
topics.reason: Rows on predicate grammar, Form IV participle, availing/sufficiency semantics, relief-from relation, and expected failure are preserved with wealth narrowed out as the local sense.

words.gloss_range: separation/behalf relation in the relief question, locally oriented around the first-person plural
words.prose: {{ar:عَنْ}} ({{tr:ʿan}}) supplies the separation and behalf relation after the availing predicate. It makes the requested help concrete: the weak ask whether anything can be moved away from us, before the later despair phrase turns the pressure upon us.

topics.headline: relief away from us
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the weak want punishment turned away from them, a relation later reversed into burden upon us.
topics.reason: Rows on the separation preposition, first-person plural chain, relief relation, and later echo with the upon-us phrase are coherent.

words.gloss_range: first min introducing the source or portion of punishment from which relief is sought
words.prose: {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) introduces the punishment domain as source or portion in the relief phrase. It begins a sequence of min-particles that move from partitive relief, to minimal possible thing, to the final denial of any escape.

topics.headline: even part of punishment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the request is reduced from rescue in general to relief from some portion of punishment.
topics.reason: Rows on governance of punishment, partitive/source force, reduced request, and the three-min sequence all survive.

words.gloss_range: construct head naming punishment as the domain from which relief is requested
words.root_gloss_range: punishment against a wider sweetness/palatability counterfield; local sense is punitive severity
words.prose: {{ar:عَذَابِ}} ({{tr:ʿadhābi}}) is the construct head in the punishment phrase, governed after the preceding min and attached to the divine name. The root’s sweetness counterfield remains only as lexical pressure; locally the word names punitive severity as the object-domain of the rescue question.

topics.headline: punishment as relief-domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the question is not abstract help; it is help against the punishment attached to God.
topics.reason: Rows on construct grammar, punishment semantics, divine-name pairing, and surah warning context are retained with non-punishment branches narrowed.

words.gloss_range: divine proper name in genitive as possessor/source in the punishment construct
words.root_gloss_range: proper-name field; local grammar is genitive second term of construct
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}) stands as the genitive second term of the punishment construct. This second divine-name occurrence centers the rescue question on divine punishment between the opening exposure before God and the later counterfactual guidance by God.

topics.headline: punishment attached to God
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the punishment in question is explicitly attached to God, not merely to circumstance or hostile leaders.
topics.reason: Rows on genitive case, construct relation, second divine-name occurrence, and exposure-punishment-guidance frame all support the topic.

words.gloss_range: second min functioning as scope amplifier before the minimal indefinite object
words.prose: {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) is not another source marker like the previous min. Before the indefinite minimum, it amplifies scope in a rhetorical question that expects failure: can you avail us from punishment by any thing whatsoever?

topics.headline: scope narrowed to anything at all
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the question pushes relief down to the smallest conceivable unit: anything at all.
topics.reason: Rows on extra/specificatory force, scope amplification, relation to the first min, and maximal negative expectation cohere.

words.gloss_range: maximally general indefinite object of possible relief
words.root_gloss_range: thingness with wider willing/bringing-into-being associations; local use selects an unspecified thing
words.prose: {{ar:شَىْءٍۢ}} ({{tr:shayʾin}}) closes the weak party’s question as an indefinite genitive minimum. The broad root can reach wider notions of thingness and willing, but the local force is maximal generality: any thing whatsoever that might count as relief.

topics.headline: anything whatsoever
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices how low the request has fallen: the weak ask whether the leaders can provide even one unspecified thing.
topics.reason: Rows on indefiniteness, genitive after min, maximal generality, and question closure are preserved, with broader root associations narrowed to unspecified thingness.

words.gloss_range: plural speech verb opening the arrogant party’s reply
words.root_gloss_range: saying and speech-report; local use introduces the leaders’ direct response
words.prose: {{ar:قَالُوا۟}} ({{tr:qālū}}) answers the earlier speech verb with a plural form. The arrogant speakers are not restated because the dialogue supplies them, and the verb opens their counterfactual explanation and no-escape admission.

topics.headline: plural counter-speech
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the answer comes as a collective reply from the leaders, matching and reversing the weak party’s earlier speech.
topics.reason: Rows on qāla/qālū echo, plural form, omitted subject, direct-response structure, and transition into counterfactual speech all align.

words.gloss_range: counterfactual particle opening an unreal condition whose answer is marked later by lām
words.prose: {{ar:لَوْ}} ({{tr:law}}) opens a counterfactual condition, not an ordinary future possibility. It sets the leaders’ reply inside an unreal guidance chain: if God had guided us, then we would have guided you.

topics.headline: unreal guidance condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the leaders’ defense begins with an unreal condition: their guidance of followers depended on God first guiding them.
topics.reason: Rows on imtināʿ condition, law/la pairing, unreal force, divine guidance as condition, and despair sequence are preserved.

words.gloss_range: perfect verb with first-person plural object: God guiding us
words.root_gloss_range: guidance, leading, and gift/offering associations; local sense is directional divine guidance
words.prose: {{ar:هَدَىٰنَا}} ({{tr:hadānā}}) names the unreal first step in the chain: God guiding us. The root’s gift and offering associations remain background; locally it is directional divine guidance received by the leaders, before any claimed guidance could pass to followers.

topics.headline: God as first guide
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the leaders make divine guidance the prior condition of any human guidance they could have given.
topics.reason: Rows on subject/object grammar, first-person object suffix, guidance semantics, surah guidance field, and the first half of the h-d-y pair survive with non-guidance branches narrowed.

words.gloss_range: nominative divine proper name as subject of the guidance verb
words.root_gloss_range: proper-name field; local grammar is nominative subject of the guidance verb
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:Allāhu}}) is the nominative subject of the guidance verb. This third divine-name occurrence closes the ayah’s divine frame by assigning the decisive act of guidance to God before the leaders speak of guiding anyone else.

topics.headline: God named as guide
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that guidance is grammatically assigned first to God, not to the leaders who had claimed status.
topics.reason: Rows on nominative case, subject function, third divine-name occurrence, and exposure-punishment-guidance frame support the topic.

words.gloss_range: answer-lām marking the apodosis of the counterfactual condition
words.prose: {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) marks the answer-clause of the counterfactual. Its force is not ordinary preposition here; it locks the second guidance verb to the unreal condition opened by the earlier particle.

topics.headline: counterfactual answer marker
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the tight law/la frame: the leaders’ claimed guidance of others is only the unreal answer to an unreal condition.
topics.reason: Rows on answer-lām function, law/la pairing, apodosis force, and sound echo are all locally supported.

words.gloss_range: perfect verb with leaderly subject and follower object, echoing the previous guidance verb
words.root_gloss_range: guidance and leading; local use repeats the guidance root with changed agency
words.prose: {{ar:هَدَيْنَٰكُمْ}} ({{tr:hadaynākum}}) repeats the guidance root with changed agency and object. The morphology fuses leaderly we with follower you, preserving the hierarchy even as the reply admits that the chain failed because divine guidance was absent in the counterfactual.

topics.headline: derivative human guidance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the hierarchy embedded in the grammar: God would guide us, and only then would we guide you.
topics.reason: Rows on object marking, first-person plural subject, second-person plural object, root echo, agency shift, and guidance-chain hierarchy all support the topic.

words.gloss_range: predicate of equivalence over the following whether/or alternatives
words.root_gloss_range: equality, leveling, fashioning, and settling; local sense is equalized outcome
words.prose: {{ar:سَوَآءٌ}} ({{tr:sawāʾun}}) functions as the predicate over the coming whether/or disjunction. The root’s broader leveling and ordering field is narrowed here to equivalence: panic and patience are laid on the same plane of futility, like equalized-outcome constructions at (2:6) and (63:6).

topics.headline: panic and patience leveled
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the word levels panic and patience into the same futile outcome, echoing equalized-outcome constructions at (2:6) and (63:6).
topics.reason: Rows on predicate grammar, tanwīn, panic/patience collapse, root leveling, idiom, and despair-to-no-escape movement are preserved with broad branches narrowed.

words.gloss_range: upon-us phrase attaching equivalence as an imposed condition on the speakers
words.prose: {{ar:عَلَيْنَآ}} ({{tr:ʿalaynā}}) attaches the equivalence to the speakers as something upon them. It reverses the earlier request for removal from us into a burden upon us, so the same collective voice moves from asking for relief to admitting imposed futility.

topics.headline: equivalence imposed upon us
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that futility is not abstract; it lies upon the speakers as their imposed condition.
topics.reason: Rows on ʿalā pressure, first-person plural suffix, echo with the earlier from-us phrase, and imposed condition are coherent.

words.gloss_range: perfect first-person plural panic verb opened by hamzat al-taswiya
words.root_gloss_range: panic, impatience, and fracture; local sense is collective panic inside a whether-frame
words.prose: {{ar:أَجَزِعْنَآ}} ({{tr:ajaziʿnā}}) opens the whether/or frame with the panic verb itself. The root’s fracture pressure gives emotional collapse a bodily undertone, while the perfect first-person plural form makes panic a collective option; its rarity and relation to (70:20) sharpen the moment where panic is declared useless.

topics.headline: panic folded into whether-frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that panic is named as one side of the futile pair, with a fracture undertone and a marked rarity sharpened by the comparison with (70:20).
topics.reason: Rows on hamzat al-taswiya, panic/fracture semantics, first-person plural form, sound opening, rarity, and the (70:20) comparison are preserved with nonlocal root associations narrowed.

words.gloss_range: disjunctive connector completing the hamza-am whether construction
words.prose: {{ar:أَمْ}} ({{tr:am}}) completes the hamza-am construction by connecting the second alternative to the first. It binds panic and patience into one whether-frame, so their semantic opposition remains visible even as equivalence cancels any difference in outcome.

topics.headline: patience bound to panic
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the connector preserves the real contrast between panic and patience only to have both alternatives equalized.
topics.reason: Rows on muʿādila function, antithetical verbs, binary emotional contrast, and equalization by the preceding predicate all support the topic.

words.gloss_range: perfect first-person plural endurance verb, paired with panic and neutralized by equivalence
words.root_gloss_range: patience, binding, restraint, and bitter endurance; local sense is collective endurance made futile
words.prose: {{ar:صَبَرْنَا}} ({{tr:ṣabarnā}}) supplies the second side of the emotional pair. The root’s binding, restraint, and bitterness make patience feel like active self-control, but the equivalence clause nullifies its salvific value here; a virtue praised at (2:153) and (3:200) is now equal to panic in outcome.

topics.headline: restraint no longer opens escape
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the devastating inversion: even patience, normally praised at (2:153) and (3:200), is made equal to panic once punishment has arrived.
topics.reason: Rows on perfect plural form, root restraint, virtue inversion, recurrence in endurance contexts, antonym pairing with panic, and moral-binary collapse are preserved with the broad virtue field locally narrowed.

words.gloss_range: negative particle opening the final existential no-escape clause
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) begins the final negated existential clause. After counterfactual guidance and equalized emotional options, this negation seals the reply by denying the availability of any escape.

topics.headline: final denial begins
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the reply ends not with advice but with negated existence: no escape is available.
topics.reason: Rows on nominal-clause negation, absolute scope with later min, final-clause opening, and closure on escape all support the topic.

words.gloss_range: possession/existential lām relation focused on the first-person plural in the no-escape clause
words.prose: {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) carries the possession/existential relation in the final no-escape claim. The local phrase turns attention from leader/follower blame to shared deprivation: nothing that could count as an escape belongs to us.

topics.headline: no escape belongs to us
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the inversion from former relation to you into final dispossession for us.
topics.reason: Rows on existential possession, first-person plural chain, total dispossession, and echo with the earlier leader-oriented lām survive, while suffix-specific wording is handled as phrase-level force.

words.gloss_range: extra/scope-marking min under negation before the no-escape noun
words.prose: {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) stands under negation before the final no-escape noun, making the denial exhaustive. It completes the ayah’s min sequence: requested relief from punishment, any minimal thing, and finally no escape whatsoever.

topics.headline: no escape whatsoever
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final negation is made exhaustive: not one instance of escape remains.
topics.reason: Rows on extra min under negation, scope blocking, the three-min progression, and final rhetorical closure are all preserved.

words.gloss_range: indefinite no-escape noun naming any place or means of turning away
words.root_gloss_range: turning aside, slipping away, refuge, and escape; local form names an escape point that negation abolishes
words.prose: {{ar:مَّحِيصٍۢ}} ({{tr:maḥīṣin}}) closes the ayah with an indefinite noun of escape after negating min. The form can name a place or point of turning aside, so the denial is spatial as well as existential: no unnamed outlet remains; the same no-escape formula appears at (4:121) and (42:35).

topics.headline: no place to turn aside
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah closes spatially: there is no unnamed place or route to swerve away, a no-escape formula also found at (4:121) and (42:35).
topics.reason: Rows on genitive indefiniteness, mafʿil place pattern, turning-aside semantics, rarity, no-escape formula, sound texture, and final scene closure are preserved with the root narrowed to local escape/refuge.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The opening emergence and total gathering at words 1 and 3 frame the weak, the self-exalting, and the followers at words 5, 7, and 11.
baseline_models.mechanism: Uncovering and total gathering move a stratified group into one public field. The dialogue then exposes the hierarchy's hidden bargain: weakness attached itself to self-magnified leadership and expected protection in return.

activation_trace.role: Coming into visibility supplies the shift from concealed social claims to exposed accountability.
Undivided totality places every rank in the same complete assembly.
Lack of strength supplies the lower pole of the social dependency.
Human self-exaltation supplies the claimed upper pole whose protective value is tested.
Following behind makes the weak party's attachment to the leaders operational rather than merely descriptive.

changed_reading.before: All parties appear, and weak followers ask arrogant leaders for help.
changed_reading.after: The appearance is an audit of a social hierarchy: exposure makes visible the protection bargain that had linked weakness, self-exaltation, and following.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The sequence from being followers, to asking whether the leaders can suffice, to the doubled guidance counterfactual occurs at words 11, 14, 23, and 25.
baseline_models.mechanism: The followers expect both substitutive protection and direction from those ahead of them. The leaders' counterfactual admits that their downstream guidance was never autonomous: the relay could transmit only what it first received.

activation_trace.role: Trailing and taking another as precedent supplies the downstream position in the relay.
Capacity to suffice or stand in for another defines the protection the followers expected.
Gentle direction to a way supplies the content that would have had to pass through the leaders.
The one going ahead supplies the spatial model of a guide whose followers take their direction from the front.

changed_reading.before: The leaders excuse their failure to help by saying that they themselves were not guided.
changed_reading.after: Their answer discloses a failed relay: the followers had mistaken an intermediate, dependent guide for an independent source of direction and protection.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The equality construction joins panic and endurance at words 26, 28, and 30, and the closing denial of any deviation or escape rests on word 34.
baseline_models.mechanism: Panic interrupts endurance while patience restrains panic, so they are normally opposed operations. The equality construction plus the absence of any lateral exit makes them outcome-equivalent inside a terminal enclosure.

activation_trace.role: Equalization removes any difference in result between the two response modes.
The breaking-off of endurance supplies one affective strategy at the endpoint.
Self-restraint against panic supplies the opposite strategy whose result is nevertheless equalized.
The unavailable sideways turn closes the spatial route by which either strategy could alter the outcome.
Entrapment and confused constriction turn the final clause into a bounded terminal state.

changed_reading.before: The condemned say that panic and patience are equally useless because there is no escape.
changed_reading.after: The verse models a terminal state in which opposed internal operations cannot produce a different transition because every lateral route is closed.

context_deltas.mechanism: Earlier outward movement is authorized and directional: people are brought out toward illumination. The focus opening repeats outwardness without that destination, converting a possible rescued exit into compulsory exposure.

activation_trace.role: Visibility after concealment anchors the focus movement as exposure.
Passing outward supplies an earlier movement with a stated destination and purpose.
Illumination gives that earlier exit a positive endpoint rather than mere visibility.
Causing something to come out repeats the rescue-shaped outward transition at the communal scale.
The repeated luminous destination fixes the contrast with the focus scene's bare exposure.

structural_cues: 14:1 and 14:5 each use a from-to construction for outward movement, while 14:21 opens with emergence before God and total assembly.
The focus emergence is immediately followed by failed protection rather than by a traversable path.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two purposive exits toward illumination and one final emergence into assembly. I infer a reversal from offered rescue to compulsory exposure; the live alternative is that the shared outward imagery marks scene transition without a deliberate contrast.

changed_reading.before: The opening simply stages everyone appearing for judgment.
changed_reading.after: Their appearance is the terminal inversion of an earlier offered exodus: those not carried outward toward illumination are finally brought out only to be uncovered.

context_deltas.mechanism: Before the endpoint, guidance opens routes and trust lets endurance continue under harm; patience therefore has directional work. Once the focus clause declares no route of deviation, patience and panic cease to differ in outcome without becoming morally or functionally identical in every phase.

activation_trace.role: Outcome equality anchors the terminal comparison.
The missing turn explains why the response modes cannot now lead to different destinations.
Sustained restraint appears earlier as a receptive capacity paired with signs and gratitude.
Received direction supplies an open route before the terminal scene.
An extended traversable way makes guidance operational rather than abstract.
Restraint under injury functions as continued movement on that way.
Reliance supplies the support that keeps pre-terminal endurance from being mere immobility.

structural_cues: 14:12 sequences received guidance, plural ways, promised endurance under injury, and repeated reliance.
14:21 instead sequences equality of reactions and the categorical absence of an exit.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies productive patience while routes remain open and equalized patience after no route remains. I infer phase-sensitive efficacy; the live alternative is that the focus speakers express only their own despair and make no broader temporal distinction.

changed_reading.before: The focus statement sounds like a blanket claim that patience is no better than panic.
changed_reading.after: It is a terminal-state diagnosis: patience had work while guidance and a way were available, but it cannot be retrofitted into an escape after the route closes.

context_deltas.mechanism: The whole-earth collective cannot affect divine self-sufficiency, while the gathered human leaders cannot suffice even minimally for their followers. The later request-and-gift sequence further separates the actual source of provision from the patrons to whom the weak had outsourced need.

activation_trace.role: Sufficing for another defines the capability being demanded from the leaders.
Complete assembly ensures that no reserve of human rank remains outside the failed test.
The earlier all-inclusive human collective supplies the maximum scale against which sufficiency is measured.
Independence from need supplies the unconditioned sufficiency that the human patrons only appeared to possess.
Giving supplies the actual upstream movement of provision.
Requesting links human need to the source that can answer it, contrasting with the failed appeal in the focus.

structural_cues: 14:8 combines an all-earth collective with divine freedom from need; 14:21 combines total assembly with a failed request that leaders suffice.
14:34 places comprehensive giving before ungrateful human response, while the focus places a request before confessed incapacity.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated collectives, two uses of the sufficiency root, and a later request-gift relation. I infer that the focus audits counterfeit patronal sufficiency; the live alternative is a narrower contrast of capacities without a critique of patronage.

changed_reading.before: The followers ask powerful people for any available relief.
changed_reading.after: The request exposes a category error: they had treated dependent human rank as if it possessed the needlessness and provisioning capacity that the surah assigns upstream.

context_deltas.mechanism: The adjacent account decomposes false leadership into invitation and response rather than coercive possession, then redirects blame to the responding selves. The closing account settles each self for its own acquisition, so collective following creates influence and liability without merging agents into one account.

activation_trace.role: Following another anchors the causal relation that the later sequence decomposes.
A consequence that clings to a person keeps liability visible inside the relation.
Denied governing power removes coercive control as the sole explanation for the following.
A verbal summons supplies the initiating action in the influence circuit.
Answering speech supplies the followers' active uptake rather than passive ownership.
Censure redirects the attempted transfer of blame toward the responders.
The self as the very person fixes the accountable unit after the social chain is traced.
Matching action with recompense supplies the final settlement rule.
What each agent acquired supplies the individually attributable balance.

structural_cues: 14:11 already distinguishes messengerhood from independent authority and places action under permission.
14:22 orders no authority, invitation, response, blame, and selves; 14:51 orders each self, acquisition, and reckoning.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an explicit invitation-response sequence and an individual settlement rule. I infer that the followers' plea attempts an invalid total transfer of agency; the live alternative is that active response does not erase manipulation or the leaders' separate responsibility.

changed_reading.before: The weak blame the leaders because they followed them.
changed_reading.after: Their claim is an attempted account transfer: the context preserves the leaders' causal invitation but also identifies the followers' response and keeps each self's acquired liability distinct.

context_deltas.mechanism: Works are converted into a particulate residue and dispersed by violent air, after which their owners have no operative capacity over what they acquired. This material sequence explains the focus leaders' inability to transfer even the smallest usable remainder to their followers.

activation_trace.role: The requested capacity to substitute or help anchors the failed transfer.
The unrestricted minimal object makes the request test whether any usable remainder exists.
Combustion residue supplies a form of accumulated work that has lost cohesion.
Moving air supplies the carrier that removes the residue from control.
Violent dispersal supplies the force that makes recovery impossible.
Effective power or ownership is explicitly denied over the dispersed result.
Acquired benefit supplies the stock that would otherwise be available for transfer.
The same unrestricted object term marks the total failure to retain anything actionable.

structural_cues: 14:18 moves from works, to ash, to violent wind, to denied capacity over earnings, to no thing.
14:21 asks whether the leaders can suffice against punishment in respect of any thing.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a material dispersal simile and a repeated no-capacity/no-thing construction. I infer de-assetization as the reason no aid can be transferred; the live alternative is that the simile concerns works generally and is not meant to model the leader-follower exchange.

changed_reading.before: The leaders simply lack enough power to help.
changed_reading.after: The expected protective assets have become non-recoverable and non-transferable: the hierarchy reaches the focus scene with no coherent remainder it can liquidate for its dependents.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context attributes a destination-setting function to corrupt leaders: they cause their people to occupy ruin and redirect them from a path toward fire. Their focus counterfactual therefore sounds less like neutral inability and more like the exposure of an inverse guidance that successfully delivered followers to the wrong terminus.

activation_trace.role: Following behind anchors the group whose destination depends on those ahead.
A guide at the front supplies the destination-setting office the speakers had claimed.
The absent turn marks arrival at a terminus from which their earlier direction cannot be corrected.
Causing occupation of a place supplies the leaders' active placement of the group.
A constituted people supplies the collective carried into the destination.
Ruin supplies the condition of the destination in which the people are installed.
Loss of right direction supplies the active inverse of guidance.
The traversable way supplies what the misdirection turns people away from.
Movement into a final outcome supplies the endpoint of the misleading route.

structural_cues: 14:28 grammatically gives the changers of blessing an active role in bringing their people into the abode of ruin.
14:30 joins manufactured rivals, misdirection from a way, temporary enjoyment, and a stated final destination.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies leaders who place a people in ruin and actors who misdirect from a way. I infer that these functions illuminate the arrogant speakers' relay; the live alternative is that the contextual actors are broader exemplars and need not be identical to every speaker in 14:21.

changed_reading.before: The leaders say they could not guide because they were not guided.
changed_reading.after: Their answer is ironically inverted: as social guides they did transmit direction, but it was destination-producing misdirection that installed their followers where no turn remains.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context marks a before-time for outgoing provision and a day on which neither exchange nor intimate alliance operates. The followers' appeal then reads as an attempt to cash a patronal bond after the transfer mechanisms that could make one party suffice for another have closed.

activation_trace.role: Standing in for another supplies the transfer the followers seek.
A consequence clinging to the relation supplies the debt-like expectation behind the appeal.
Value leaving one's possession supplies an available transfer before the deadline.
Exchange for a countervalue supplies one mechanism explicitly unavailable on that day.
Intimate attachment supplies the social mechanism that is also unavailable.

structural_cues: 14:31 contrasts spending before the day with the absence of both sale and intimate alliance within it.
14:21 stages an appeal from dependents to patrons after everyone has entered the terminal assembly.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a temporal closure of economic and intimate transfers. I infer that the focus request tries to redeem expired social credit; the live alternative is that the no-sale/no-alliance warning is general and not specifically transactionalizing this follower relation.

changed_reading.before: The followers make a desperate personal request of former allies.
changed_reading.after: They try too late to convert loyalty into protection, but both the exchange channel and the alliance channel through which that social credit might pay out are closed.

context_deltas.mechanism: One contextual following relation makes the follower part of the speaker's own circle and places the non-follower under forgiveness and mercy. The focus relation instead uses service toward patrons and ends in failed reciprocity, exposing a claim of belonging that the arrogant never truly carry.

activation_trace.role: Adherence to a precedent anchors the followers' claim on the leaders.
Expected sufficiency tests whether the claimed relation includes reciprocal care.
Following here supplies a contrasting relation explicitly joined to inclusion in the speaker's own circle.
Departure from obedience supplies the relation's outside case without turning it into patronal retaliation.
Merciful tenderness supplies a non-transactional horizon for the one who does not follow.

structural_cues: 14:36 places following, being of the speaker, disobedience, forgiveness, and mercy in one relational statement.
14:21 places being followers for the leaders, a demand for protective sufficiency, and the leaders' refusal in one exchange.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two differently framed following relations. I infer that the focus dative carries a failed expectation of patronal belonging; the live alternative is that the prepositional contrast is stylistic and does not by itself encode two social systems.

changed_reading.before: The weak merely report that they used to follow the arrogant.
changed_reading.after: Their wording presses a membership claim: service had made them expect incorporation and care, but the reply reveals a patronage relation that accepts followers without carrying them.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later scene repeats emergence after the world itself is substituted, then names singular, overpowering sovereignty. Read back into the focus, total gathering is not only co-presence but recomposition of many ranked relations before the one power that makes every patronal claim derivative.

activation_trace.role: Complete totality supplies the many whose internal ranks are brought into one field.
Claimed human grandeur supplies the rank that the later asymmetry relativizes.
One order standing in place of another supplies cosmic-scale removal of the former social setting.
The repeated coming into visibility identifies the focus opening with the transformed-world assembly.
Sovereignty without partner supplies the singular pole opposite the gathered many.
Dominance from above supplies the only effective hierarchy left in the scene.

structural_cues: 14:48 sequences world substitution, repeated emergence before God, singularity, and overpowering dominance.
14:21 sequences emergence, totality, and the collapse of the weak/arrogant hierarchy's protective function.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a repeated emergence formula and an explicit many-to-one asymmetry after cosmic change. I infer social flattening within that asymmetry; the live alternative is that the later formula merely locates the same eschatological scene without commenting on rank.

changed_reading.before: All ranks happen to stand together before judgment.
changed_reading.after: The gathering actively strips rank of independent force: the many are recomposed before singular sovereignty, so the arrogant can no longer function as an upper tier for the weak.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it extends a legal-existential lack of escape into bodily orientation. It remains anchored in the focus root for lateral deviation and in the packet's fixed gaze, directed head, failed return, and emptied heart; downstream prose should present it as an embodied overlay, not as the exclusive sense of the closing clause.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus closes with no lateral deviation at word 34 after panic and patience have been equalized.

activation_trace.role: A turn away or aside supplies the motor possibility explicitly denied in the focus.
A gaze locked upward supplies visual fixation rather than free scanning.
The directed neck and head supply bodily alignment under constraint.
Failure of return removes the ordinary reversal of the gaze.
The eye's momentary turn supplies the orienting reflex that no longer comes back.
Loss of effective inward heart supplies affective vacancy alongside the motor lock.

changed_reading.before: No escape means that no external refuge is available.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, no escape is also enacted inside the body: gaze, head, return reflex, and heart no longer furnish even an orienting turn.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is branch-distant because total gathering normally states universality, not restraint. It remains worth carrying because the focus inventory itself includes a binding branch for gathering, following carries a clinging consequence, and 14:49 materially joins people in fetters; downstream prose should mark the carceral reading as an exploratory concretization of social attachment.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus combines total gathering at word 3 with the followers' attachment and its consequence at word 11.

activation_trace.role: A restraint that joins limbs supplies a materially coercive edge to being gathered.
A consequence that remains attached supplies continuity from chosen following to inescapable liability.
Joining one thing to another supplies the physical realization of relational coupling.
Binding restraint supplies the carceral medium in which the coupling appears.

changed_reading.before: Everyone is simply present together while former followers argue with leaders.
changed_reading.after: As an exploratory material overlay, the social bond has hardened into enforced conjunction: the attachment that organized following now gathers its participants as a liability they cannot separate from.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the packet's secondary h-d-d mapping rather than the ordinary guidance sense of the surface form. The split target is explicitly preserved and the surrounding stable-word versus uprooted-word sequence gives the structural break a live mechanism; downstream prose must never translate the guidance verb as demolition and should label this only as a branch-echo of relay collapse.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The doubled guidance form at words 23 and 25 carries both the ordinary leading target and the packet's secondary structural-break target.

activation_trace.role: A guide going in front supplies the relay structure asserted by the counterfactual.
Severe structural breaking supplies the packet-preserved echo of that relay's collapse.
Persistence supplies the contrasting condition of a sound rooted communication structure.
Removal of the whole thing from its root supplies structural failure rather than mere bad content.
Denied stability supplies the missing base from which a relay could continue.
Speech as a held position supplies the communicative structure whose stability matters.
Strengthening supplies the alternative to a guidance chain that cannot support transmission.

changed_reading.before: The leaders describe an ordinary guidance relay that never received an upstream signal.
changed_reading.after: As a contained branch-echo, the counterfactual also sounds like a demolished relay: unlike stable rooted speech, their leader-to-follower structure has no base capable of carrying direction.

strongest_changes: The focus emergence became the terminal inversion of earlier guided exits toward illumination.
Patience became phase-sensitive: effective while guidance and paths remain open, outcome-equivalent to panic only after every turn closes.
Human leadership became counterfeit sufficiency and a failed relay whose invitation, response, and individual accounts remain distinguishable.
The leaders' claim of failed guidance was inverted by the context's destination-setting leaders who place their people in ruin and misdirect them from a way.
The repeated emergence before singular overpowering sovereignty flattened the weak/arrogant hierarchy's claim to independent force.
summary.what_was_special: The whole-surah packet turned a short courtroom exchange into an audit of relational infrastructure: routes, relay, provision, exchange, belonging, destination, and liability all close, invert, or become individually accountable at exposure.
remaining_uncertainties: The destination-setting actors of 14:28-30 illuminate the focus hierarchy functionally, but the packet does not identify every focus speaker with those actors.
The belonging contrast with 14:36 is structurally suggestive, but the prepositional difference alone cannot bear the whole social model.
The bodily lock, carceral gathering, and secondary h-d-d activation should remain explicitly exploratory rather than become lexical translations.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Exposure collapses delegated social strength.** `ب ر ز` `B001` (becoming exposed), `ض ع ف` `B001` (lack of strength), `ك ب ر` `B006` (self-magnification), `ت ب ع` `B003` (stepwise tracking), and `غ ن ي` `B002` (availing/sufficing) map hierarchy as a failed protection chain. The packet supplies followers' dependence and leaders' admission; I infer social rank had functioned as borrowed sufficiency until collective exposure removed its cover. The scene reads as liquidation of delegated agency.

2. **Panic and patience become equal only after all routes close.** `ج ز ع` `B003` is collapse of patience, `ص ب ر` `B001` its restraint, and `ح ي ص` `B001` turning aside from a course plus `B002` a tight bewildering bind. Earlier patience kept messengers on known paths; here “no turning place” removes the future toward which restraint could work. I infer the equivalence is situational, not a general devaluation of patience. The ayah sharply distinguishes patience before closure from patience after consequence.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: The speech of 14:22 completes the hierarchy's collapse by refusing both blame-transfer and reciprocal rescue; social following never became shared coercive power.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Exposure removes the shelter of hierarchy.** `ب ر ز B001` supplies appearing and becoming exposed, `ج م ع B002` an assembled multitude, and `ض ع ف B001` lack of strength. After hidden consequences lay `وَرَاء` in 14:16-17 and works dispersed in 14:18, all now appear together, but their weak/arrogant distinction remains unable to shelter anyone. The packet supplies exposure and failed rank; I infer that appearing before God strips hierarchy of protective function. `بَرَزُوا لِلَّهِ جَمِيعًا` reads as social relations made fully inspectable.
2. **Following creates liability that cannot be transferred upward.** `ت ب ع B001` supplies following after, while `ت ب ع B006` supplies incurred liability. The followers ask the leaders to absorb some punishment; 14:22 then has the inviter deny coercion and redirect blame to the respondents themselves. The packet supplies following, attempted transfer, and later refusal; I infer that voluntary following attaches consequence to the follower. `تَبَعًا` thus describes a causal-legal relation, not mere social proximity.
3. **All behavioral alternatives collapse at a closed endpoint.** `س و ي B001` supplies equality, `ج ز ع B003` collapse of patience, `ص ب ر B001` restraint from panic, and `ح ي ص B002` a tight bewildering bind. Panic and restraint ordinarily diverge, but the negated escape makes them equal with respect to outcome. The packet gives the alternatives and closure; I infer that endpoint topology, not moral equivalence, neutralizes their difference. `سَوَاءٌ عَلَيْنَا` reads as terminal equalization inside a no-exit condition.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 14:22 corrected the followers' attempted liability transfer by denying coercion and returning blame to respondents. It made `تَبَعًا` an incurred relation, while 14:23's peaceful greeting exposed the opposite kind of social bond.

baseline.text: Hepsi Allah'ın huzuruna çıktığında güçsüzler büyüklük taslayanlara, “Biz size uymuştuk; şimdi Allah'ın azabından bir kısmını bizden savabilir misiniz?” derler. Onlar, “Allah bize doğru yolu gösterseydi biz de size gösterirdik. Sızlansak da sabretsek de bizim için birdir; kaçacak yerimiz yok” derler.

findings.text: Toplu açığa çıkış, toplumsal hiyerarşinin koruyucu örtüsünü kaldırır ve ödünç alınmış gücü tasfiye eder.
Gönüllü izleyiş, sonucu üstteki lidere aktarılamayan bir sorumluluğu izleyene yükler.
Kaçış yolu bütünüyle kapandığında sızlanma ile sabır yalnız sonuç bakımından eşitlenir; bu, yol açıkken sabrın değerini geçersiz kılmaz.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bir şeyin gizlilikten çıkıp görünmesi ile bir şeyi görünür kılmayı aynı anlam çekirdeğinde toplar. Kitap için görünür ya da yayımlanmış olma, bu çekirdeğin sözlüksel olarak sınırlı bir gerçekleşmesidir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Genel çekirdek görünür olma veya kılmadır; kitapla ilgili yayımlanma yorumu bütün kullanımlara yayılmaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, yalın görünme anlamını korurken ettirgen biçimleri ve kitapla sınırlı yayımlanma kullanımını ayrı tutar.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyin gizliyken ortaya çıkıp görünür olması veya üzerindeki örtünün kalkması; ettirgen kullanımlarda bir şeyi ya da kitabı görünür kılmaktır. Kitap nitelemesinde ayrıca yayımlanmış olma anlamı bulunur.

facets.statement: Bir şey kendiliğinden gizlilikten çıkar, belirir ve görünür olur.
Bir kişi bir şeyi görünür duruma getirir, açıkça gösterir veya belirginleştirir.
Kitapla ilgili türemiş kullanımlarda görünür olmanın yanında yayımlanmış olma yorumu da vardır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar görünme, gizlilikten çıkma ve görünür kılma çekirdeğinde birleşir. Kitap nitelemesinde görünür olma açıklamasının yanında bazı aktarımlar yayımlanmış olma yorumunu verir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Hem kendiliğinden belirme çekirdeğini hem de bir şeyi görünür kılan ettirgen uzantıyı birlikte karşılar.

error_profile.preserves: Belirme, açığa çıkma ve görünür kılma ayrımını korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Gizli ya da örtülü bir şeyin kendiliğinden görünür olduğu cümlelerde kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Gizlilikten görünürlüğe geçişi doğal bir eylemle anlatır.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir kişinin bir şeyi görünür kıldığı veya belirginleştirdiği ettirgen bağlamlara uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Ettirgen görünür kılma işlemini ve sonucu korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Yalnızca kitap nitelemesindeki yayıma çıkarılmış olma yorumunda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Kitaba bağlı özel yayımlanma yorumunu korur.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal, kitap için görünür kılma ve yayımlanmış olma kullanımını da kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal, görünüşteki kanaat veya ilk bakışta beliren görüş kullanımına da uzanır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da gizli bir şeyin görünmesini ve bir şeyin görünür kılınmasını anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Ortak görünme çekirdeğine rağmen odak dalın kitapla sınırlı sözlüksel uzantısı ile komşunun kanaat alanındaki uzantısı birbirinin yerine kullanılamaz.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal ettirgen görünür kılmayı ve kitapta yayımlanmış olma yorumunu içerir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal, bir şeyin içte değil dışta ve açıkça görünür olmasını ayrıca öne çıkarır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da bir şeyin görünmesi, açılması ve belirginleşmesi alanında örtüşür.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Komşu daha çok görünür durumda bulunmayı anlatırken odak dal görünme sürecini, ettirgen göstermeyi ve kitap kullanımını birlikte taşır.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Adayların tümü karşılaştırıldı; dalın sınırını en açık gösteren iki yakın anlam ilişkisi seçildi.
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه ظهور الشيء بعد خفاء، وانكشاف ما كان مستورا، وإظهار الشيء أو الكتاب، والكتاب المبروز بمعنى الظاهر أو المنشور
branches.what_is_not_ar: لا يدخل فيه خصوص الفضاء الواسع، ولا المبارزة، ولا التبرز كناية عن قضاء الحاجة
branches.source_phrase_ar: أصل واحد وهو ظهور الشيء وبدوه؛ برز الشيء فهو بارز؛ أبرزت الشيء أبرزه إبرازا؛ المبروز الظاهر؛ وقال قوم المبروز المنشور (maqayis)؛ برز فلان أي ظهر بعد الخفاء؛ أبرزت الكتاب والشيء أي أظهرته؛ كتاب مبروز مبرز أي منشور (ayn)؛ برزت الشيء تبريزا أي أظهرته وبينته؛ كتاب مبروز أي منشور (sihah)؛ برز أي هو منكشف الشأن ظاهره؛ برز مخفف فمعناه ظهر بعد الخفاء (tahdhib)؛ أن يظهر بذاته؛ أن ينكشف عنه ما كان مستورا منه (mufradat)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, üstü örtülmeyen geniş araziyi ve bir kişinin böyle bir yere çıkmasını açıkça birlikte verir. Çıkma eylemi, yer adının bütün anlamını değil, o yere yönelmeyi anlatan bağımlı kullanımdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, her tür boşluğu değil, açık ve geniş araziyi ve bu araziye çıkmayı kapsar.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, açık araziyi yalın yer anlamı olarak; oraya çıkmayı ise belirli bir söz öbeğine bağlı uzantı olarak ayırır.

concept_map.definition: Çukur, oyuk veya bitki örtüsüyle kapanmamış, uzakta ve genişçe uzanan açık arazidir. Kişi için kullanıldığında böyle bir açık alana çıkmayı veya orada bulunmayı anlatır.

facets.statement: Yer, geniş, açık, görünür ve örtüsüz bir arazi parçasıdır.
Bir kişi kapalı yerden çıkarak bu açık araziye gider veya orada bulunur.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, geniş ve örtüsüz arazi anlamında ve insanın bu araziye çıkması kullanımında birleşir. Arazi, çukur ya da bitkiyle kapalı bir yerin karşıtı olarak betimlenir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Yer adının açık, örtüsüz ve geniş arazi çekirdeğini doğrudan karşılar.

error_profile.preserves: Arazinin genişliğini, açıklığını ve örtüsüzlüğünü korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir kişinin kapalı veya örtülü yerden geniş ve açık araziye yöneldiği bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Kişinin belirli türdeki açık yere çıkışını korur.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: açık araziye çıkmak veya orada bulunmak

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal, arazinin örtüsüz ve görünür olmasını ve kişinin oraya çıkmasını özellikle belirtir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal, avlu, düzlük ve genel olarak genişleyen yerleri de kapsayan daha geniş bir yer alanına sahiptir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da geniş, açık bir yeri ve açık yere çıkma düşüncesini paylaşır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal açık arazinin örtüsüzlüğünü sözlüksel sınır yaparken komşu dal genişlik ve düzlük üzerinden daha çeşitli yerleri içine alır.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar değerlendirildi; açık arazi sınırını en iyi belirleyen yakın anlamlı komşu yayımlandı.
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه البراز للفضاء الواسع المكشوف، وبروز الشخص بمعنى خروجه إلى ذلك الموضع
branches.what_is_not_ar: لا يدخل فيه التبرز كناية عن قضاء الحاجة إلا من جهة الخروج إلى البراز، ولا البرزخ الحائل بين الشيئين
branches.source_phrase_ar: البراز المتسع من الأرض لأنه باد ليس بغائط ولا دحل ولا هوة (maqayis)؛ البراز المكان الفضاء من الأرض البعيد الواسع؛ تبرز فلان خرج إلى البراز (ayn)؛ برز الرجل يبرز بروزا خرج؛ البراز بالفتح الفضاء الواسع؛ الموضع الذي ليس به خمر من شجر ولا غيره؛ تبرز الرجل أي خرج إلى البراز للحاجة (sihah)؛ البراز المكان الفضاء من الأرض البعيد الواسع؛ خرج الإنسان إلى ذلك الموضع قيل قد برز (tahdhib)؛ البراز الفضاء؛ برز حصل في براز (mufradat)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi sıradan çatışmayı değil, iki rakibin kendi topluluklarından ayrılıp birbirinin karşısına çıkarak teke tek savaşmasını kurucu anlam olarak verir. Dal çerçevesi bu katılımcı değişimini ve karşılıklılığı doğru korur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Yalnızca görünmek veya genel savaşa katılmak yetmez; rakiplerin saftan ayrılıp karşılaşması gerekir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, savaş adını ve rakiplerin karşılıklı olarak saftan çıkmasını anlatan söz öbeklerini birbirine karıştırmadan kapsar.

concept_map.definition: İki rakibin savaşmak üzere kendi saflarından veya topluluklarından ayrılıp birbirinin karşısına çıkması ve teke tek çarpışmasıdır.

facets.statement: Karşılaşma iki rakip arasında, teke tek savaşma amacıyla gerçekleşir.
Her rakip kendi topluluğundan veya safından ayrılarak ötekinin karşısına çıkar.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, iki rakibin karşılıklı biçimde saflarından ayrılıp savaşmak için yüz yüze gelmesi çekirdeğinde birleşir. Genel savaş değil, bire bir karşılaşma vurgulanır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Hem gruptan ayrılma aşamasını hem de iki rakibin karşılıklı savaşmasını birlikte karşılar.

error_profile.preserves: Ayrılma, karşı karşıya gelme ve teke tek savaşma işlemlerini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Tek bir savaşçının safından ayrılarak belirli rakibine yöneldiği cümlelerde kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Savaşçının gruptan ayrılıp rakibine yönelmesini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: İki rakibin karşılıklı ve bire bir savaşması öne çıktığında kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: İki rakipli karşılıklı savaşma yapısını korur.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: karşılıklı olarak saftan çıkıp teke tek dövüşmek

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal, her savaşçının kendi safından veya topluluğundan ayrılmasını kurucu aşama sayar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal, her savaşçının kendine denk bir rakibi üstlenmesi veya onunla buluşması biçiminde eşleşmeyi öne çıkarır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da savaşta iki rakibin bire bir karşı karşıya gelmesini anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bire bir savaş ortak olsa da odak dalın saftan ayrılma aşaması ile komşunun rakipleri eşleştirme vurgusu tam olarak aynı sınırı kurmaz.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal iki rakibin saftan ayrılarak teke tek karşılaşmasını gerektirir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal, iki veya daha çok taraf arasındaki genel savaşma ve öldürmeye yönelme alanını kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dalda tarafların savaş amacıyla birbirine karşı güç kullanması vardır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Komşu genel savaş alanını adlandırır; odak dal ise bunun içinde iki kişinin saflardan ayrıldığı özel bire bir karşılaşmayı belirtir.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Adayların tamamı incelendi; bire bir karşılaşmayı genel savaştan ayıran iki komşu seçildi.
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه البراز والمبارزة، وتبارز القرنين أو الفارسين، وخروج المقاتل من جماعته إلى صاحبه
branches.what_is_not_ar: لا يدخل فيه مجرد الظهور بلا مقابلة، ولا السبق في الفضل أو السباق
branches.source_phrase_ar: انفراد الشيء من أمثاله نحو تبارز الفارسين؛ كل واحد منهما ينفرد عن جماعته إلى صاحبه (maqayis)؛ البراز المبارزة من القرنين في الحرب؛ تبارزا؛ بارز القرن مبارزة وبرازا (ayn)؛ البراز المبارزة في الحرب (sihah)؛ المبارزة الحرب؛ البراز أخذ من هذا؛ تبارز القرنان (tahdhib)؛ المبارزة للقتال وهي الظهور من الصف (mufradat)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi hem yarışta öne geçmeyi hem de övgüye değer bir iş veya üstün nitelik sayesinde akranlarını aşmayı verir. Ortak nokta yalnızca görünmek değil, karşılaştırılanlar içinde öne çıkmaktır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, her tür görünürlüğü değil, yarış veya değer karşılaştırmasında başkalarını geçmeyi anlatır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Anlam, kişinin ya da atın başkalarına göre öne geçtiğini belirten kısıtlı yapılara bağlı tutulur.

concept_map.definition: Bir kişinin veya atın hızda öne geçmesi ya da bir kişinin övgüye değer bir iş ve üstün nitelik sayesinde akranlarını aşmasıdır.

facets.statement: Bir yarışçı, özellikle bir at, yarışta diğerlerinin önüne geçer.
Bir kişi övgüye değer işi veya niteliğiyle arkadaşlarından üstün duruma gelir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, yarışta öne geçme ile değerli bir iş veya nitelik bakımından akranlardan üstün olmayı aynı karşılaştırmalı çekirdekte toplar.

concept_gloss.applicability: Hem somut yarış üstünlüğünü hem de övgüye değer nitelikle akranları aşmayı karşılar.

error_profile.preserves: Karşılaştırmayı, öne geçmeyi ve iki temel uygulama alanını korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir insanın veya atın yarışta diğer yarışçıları geride bıraktığı bağlamlara uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Yarış içindeki karşılaştırmalı üstünlüğü korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir kişinin övgüye değer işi veya niteliğiyle çevresindekileri aştığı bağlamlara uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Değer ve nitelik bakımından başkalarını aşmayı korur.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: arkadaşlarını geride bırakmak veya onlardan üstün olmak

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal, yarışta hızla öne geçmeyi ve övgüye değer bir eylemde akranları aşmayı birlikte içerir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal güzellik, şeref, derece ve genel toplumsal konum üstünlüğüne daha geniş biçimde uzanır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da bir kişinin karşılaştırılanlardan daha yüksek veya üstün durumda olmasını anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal yarış ya da övgüye değer başarıyla gerçekleşen öne geçişi anlatırken komşu, elde edilmiş yüksek konum ve üstünlüğü daha geniş alanlarda adlandırır.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar karşılaştırıldı; yarış ile değer üstünlüğü sınırını en iyi gösteren komşu seçildi.
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه برز الرجل أو الفرس إذا سبق، وظهور الشخص بفضله أو فاق أصحابه في فعل محمود
branches.what_is_not_ar: لا يدخل فيه الخروج إلى الفضاء، ولا المبارزة في الحرب
branches.source_phrase_ar: برز الرجل والفرس إذا سبقا وهو من الباب (maqayis)؛ إذا تسابقت الخيل قيل لسابقها قد برز عليها (ayn)؛ برز الرجل أيضا فاق على أصحابه؛ وكذلك الفرس إذا سبق (sihah)؛ إذا تسابقت الخيل قيل لسابقها قد برز عليها (tahdhib)؛ أن يظهر بفضله وهو أن يسبق في فعل محمود (mufradat)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi görünür ve açık tavırlı olmayı tek başına bırakmaz; saygınlık, sağlam akıl, güvenilir görüş, temiz karakter ve iffeti birlikte verir. Kadının insanların önüne çıkıp onlarla oturabilmesi bu toplumsal görünürlüğün özel gerçekleşmesidir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal sıradan görünürlüğü değil, saygınlık, güvenilir görüş ve iffetle birleşen toplumsal açıklığı niteler.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, yalın niteleme biçimlerinin saygınlık, akıl, görünürlük ve iffet bileşimini korur.

concept_map.definition: İnsanlar önünde açıkça yer alan, saygın, aklına ve görüşüne güvenilen, temiz karakterli ve iffetli kimsedir. Kadın için özellikle insanların karşısına çıkabilen ve onların yanına oturabilen yüksek konumlu kişi anlatılır.

facets.statement: Kişi açık tavırlı, saygın ve aklına ya da görüşüne güvenilir biridir.
Kişi temiz karakterli ve iffetli olarak nitelenir.
Kadın için saygın biçimde insanların önüne çıkma ve onların yanına oturma özelliği belirtilir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar saygınlık, açıklık, sağlam akıl ve iffeti birlikte aktarır. Kadına ilişkin kullanımda güvenilir görüş ve insanların önünde saygın biçimde bulunma ayrıca belirginleşir.

concept_gloss.text: insanlar önünde saygın, güvenilir ve iffetli kimse
concept_gloss.applicability: Toplumsal görünürlüğü, saygınlığı, güvenilir aklı ve iffeti birlikte gerektiren nitelemeyi karşılar.
